chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl and she was menstruating (ṭāmith). Should he clear her womb with another menstruation, or would this menstruation suffice for him? He said: No, but this menstruation suffices this menstruation suffices for him. If he clears her with another, there is no problem; it is in the nature of preference (fadl).

key_terms.طَامِثٌ: A female who is currently menstruating
key_terms.فَضْلٍ: Preference/Virtue (in legal context, a recommended but not obligatory act)
key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئُ: To clear (the womb) by observing menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibra' for a slave girl who menstruates upon purchase?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a single menstruation suffices for the 'clearing of the womb' (istibra') of a purchased slave girl, resolving potential disputes over pregnancy status. The Imam notes that an additional menstruation is merely a preferred act (fadl) rather than a legal requirement, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the time. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease and certainty in commercial and marital transactions involving slaves.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked about a man who bought a slave girl and she menstruated. Should he clear her womb with another menstruation or would this menstruation suffice?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but this menstruation would suffice. But, if he were to clear her woman with another (menstruation), so there is no problem. It would be in a state of preference’.
